newsitem.title: USA: Chicago schools set hearing on capital bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Chicago schools set hearing on capital bond issue.

text.p: The Chicago public school system will hold a public hearing Thursday on plans to issue up to $800 million of bonds for capital projects, a school finance official said Thursday.

Chuck Burbridge, deputy chief financial officer, said school officials currently plan to sell $350 million to $500 million of alternate bonds, backed by the schools' general obligation pledge in late April in a deal led by Goldman, Sachs & Co with BA Securities as the co-manager.
The bond sale would be the second in a $1.15 billion, capital improvement program adopted by Chicago School Reform Board in January 1996. Last April, the school system sold $350 million of bonds.

Burbridge said the upcoming deal would be structured like last year's issue, with the bonds being paid off with the schools' personal property tax replacement revenues. He added that MBIA Insurance Corp was expected to provide insurance for this deal as it had done in the previous issue.
A hearing on the projects that would be funded with bond proceeds is scheduled for next week, according to Burbridge. He added that the school board would then take action on the bond issue by March.
